newsitem.title: USA: Rising consumer debt a grave concern - Fed's Lindsey.
newsitem.headline: Rising consumer debt a grave concern - Fed's Lindsey.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey Thursday called the recent steep rise in consumer debt a "matter of grave concern" and said that the consumer spending boom based on it was unsustainable.
"The level of debt and the fact that debt has been growing so quickly is a matter of grave concern for macroeconomic policymakers," Lindsey told the House Banking Committee.
"To some extent ... the consumer boom is unsustainable," he added.
Lindsey said though that it was unclear what the Fed should do about the steep rise in consumer debt. Consumers now are spending $1.10 for every one dollar they make, he said.
"On the one hand, it's our objective to make sure that we have a stabilizing role in the economy, that any downturn not be a severe one," he said.

"On the other hand, there's the proverbial "take away the punch bowl" role (for the Fed)," he said. "One might conclude that when you're spending an extra $1.10 for every dollar you're getting in a raise, that maybe a few people have had a nip or two too much."
"You have to balance those two facts in weighing the macroeconomic effects," Lindsey said.
He said that the recent economic expansion has been slow by historical standards, but added that the answer was not for the Fed to print more money.

Lindsey opposed regulatory or legislative action to force banks to cut back on their consumer loans, saying that would lead to an economic downturn. "I couldn't imagine any more effective way of causing a recession than to do that," he said.
He did though urge banks to take a "prudent look" at their loan portfolios.
